intent: Revert the body to the iteration-0 values (0.18 m long, 0.8 kg) and keep the wider ±0.03 m sensor spread at 15 mm spacing with the 4 cm forward row. This isolates the body change against iteration 2 and tests whether the spread alone keeps s-bend line loss at or below 1 while progress recovers toward 0.185. Expected: score at or above 54 and s-bend progress at or above 0.15.
learning: Iteration 2 showed that changing the body together with the sensing made the s-bend progress worse (0.185 to 0.1275) even though line loss fell to 1. This iteration tests whether the body or the spread caused the loss. If progress recovers with the baseline body, the body reduction was the cause and the lighter, shorter body should not be used. If progress stays near 0.13, the wider spread is the cause and the next test is ±0.02 at y=0.04. In both cases the integrator's sensor_size 0.016 test should wait until progress is at least 0.15 with line loss at or below 1.
rationale: Scores so far: iteration 0 = 54.3 (y=0.04, x ±0.02, 10 mm spacing, body 0.18 m x 0.12 m, 0.8 kg), iteration 1 = 36.3 (y=0.02, x ±0.03), iteration 2 = 46.4 (y=0.04, x ±0.03, body 0.14 m, 0.6 kg). Two changes in iteration 2 were made together, so I cannot yet separate their effects. The clearest signal is the s-bend: progress fell from 0.185 to 0.1275, while line-loss events dropped from 2 to 1. This suggests the wider ±0.03 spread helps line retention, and the drop in progress comes from either the 4 cm row being unchanged (so not the row) or the lighter, shorter body, which is the main suspect. The integrator's rule covers this case directly: progress is below 0.15, so I should not change sensor_size to 0.016 yet. Their conditional instruction, for progress below 0.10 with low line loss, says to revert the body to 0.18 m and 0.8 kg. Progress here is 0.1275, slightly above that threshold, but it is still well below the 0.185 seen with the baseline body, and the iteration-2 score fell. I will therefore revert the body to the iteration-0 values (length 0.18, mass 0.8) while keeping the ±0.03 spread with 15 mm spacing and the y=0.04 row. This isolates the body variable against iteration 2 and tests whether the wider spread and 4 cm row preserve the baseline's s-bend progress with fewer line losses. Wheel track, wheel radius and body width stay at their baseline values. I expect a score near or above 54, with s-bend line loss at or below 1 and progress recovering toward 0.18. If progress stays near 0.13 with the body reverted, the wider spread is the likely cause of the progress loss, and the next step is to test the ±0.02 spread at y=0.04.
